bank_plan.formula: (lesson_check_items + module_check_items) x 2 alternates + forms x form_length
bank_plan.eighty_twenty_note: 80% instruction / 20% assessment honoured at course level (I+A=T); bank serves lesson checks, module checks, 3 practice forms and a protected final.
bank_plan.size_band_note: Planning range per assessment standard (200-600 skills; 600-1500+ large certification). This is a planning guide, not proof of quality.

mcq_limitation_note: Knowledge-practice forms use MCQ/MR only; official item formats not reproducible in this format are listed in the exam-version record.

items.stem: A practitioner must choose a control that prevents a terminated employee from accessing systems the same day. Which control is most effective?

options.text: Automated deprovisioning tied to the HR termination event
options.rationale: Correct: event-driven deprovisioning removes access immediately and reliably.
Quarterly reviews leave a window of up to three months of access.
Training does not remove a departed user's access.
Password rules do not disable an existing valid account.

items.explanation: Timely, event-driven deprovisioning closes the access window immediately.

items.stem: Which cryptographic service provides proof that a specific sender created a message?

options.rationale: Correct: a digital signature binds the message to the sender's private key, giving non-repudiation.
A shared symmetric key cannot prove which party sent the message.
A bare hash gives integrity but not sender identity.
Salting strengthens stored password hashes; it is unrelated to sender proof.

items.explanation: Digital signatures provide authentication, integrity and non-repudiation of origin.

items.stem: Which TWO actions best preserve forensic evidence during incident response?

options.text: Capture a bit-for-bit image of affected storage
options.rationale: Correct: an exact image preserves the original state for analysis.

options.text: Document a chain of custody for collected evidence
options.rationale: Correct: chain of custody keeps evidence admissible and trustworthy.

options.text: Reboot the affected host to clear the malware
options.rationale: Rebooting destroys volatile memory and running-state evidence.

options.text: Edit logs to highlight the suspicious entries

options.rationale: Deleting removes evidence needed for analysis.

items.explanation: Imaging and chain of custody preserve evidence integrity and admissibility.
